judgments.title: Calvin Harris Plays Langley Park, Perth
judgments.description: Calvin Harris' first ever Australian headline tour reaches Perth, the opening night of the tour. Four cities across February 2027, with a second Perth show added the night before.
judgments.reason: Scheduled headline tour stop and added show are mildly positive for promoter; no performance outcome.

judgments.title: Longroad Allium Solar and Energy Storage: 110 MW Solar and 110 MW Battery on 945 Acres in San Benito County, California
judgments.description: Longroad Energy's Allium Solar is proposed as 110 MW of solar plus 110 MW of battery storage on about 945 acres north of Hollister airport. Aggregators list a December 2030 expected online date.
judgments.reason: Proposed development; distant aggregator date and no completed outcome.

judgments.title: TransGrid Atlas VIII Battery Storage: 382.4 MW / 1,529.6 MWh in La Paz County, Arizona, 1.2B USD Financing Closed
judgments.description: TransGrid Energy closed about $1.2 billion of financing in January 2026 for the Atlas VIII standalone battery project in La Paz County, Arizona. The project will deliver 382.4 MW / 1,529.6 MWh; the sources read give no firm completion date.
judgments.reason: Financing closed for substantial battery development.

judgments.title: Alina Energy (Anila Solar and Anila BESS): 200.8 MW Solar Plus Battery in Wilson County, Texas, Proposed for 2028
judgments.description: Alina Energy LLC has a 200.8 MW solar queue entry (ERCOT 26INR0074) and a companion battery entry (26INR0077, about 209 MW) in Wilson County, Texas. The EIA-860M record lists two generating units totalling 400 MW with a proposed completion of June 2028, while the ERCOT queue lists 30 September 2028.
judgments.reason: Proposed queue entries with conflicting dates, no operating milestone.

judgments.title: Aligned PHX-06 Data Center: Two-Phase 456,946 sq ft Campus in Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona
judgments.description: Aligned's PHX06 in Chandler is a two-phase development totaling 456,946 sq ft; the first phase topped out in June 2024. MW capacity and a Phase 2 date are not published in the sources read.
judgments.reason: First phase topped out; second-phase timing unconfirmed.

judgments.title: CleanArc VA1 Campus: 900 MW, 3B USD Hyperscale Data Center Campus in Caroline County, Virginia, First 300 MW Targeted for 2027
judgments.description: CleanArc Data Centers broke ground on its first Greater Fredericksburg campus in Caroline County, Virginia. The campus is planned at 900 MW in phases, with 300 MW expected in 2027 and full buildout in 2033 to 2035.
judgments.reason: Groundbreaking is a concrete expansion milestone, future phases uncertain.

judgments.title: AES Rt 5 Solar: 5 MW Ground-Mounted Community Solar in Le Roy, Genesee County, New York
judgments.description: AES DE DEVCO NC LLC applied for a Clean Water Act certification for a 5 MW ground-mounted solar project on West Main Road in Le Roy, Genesee County. Trackers list a proposed in-service of June to July 2026; operating status is not confirmed.
judgments.reason: Permit application with unconfirmed operation and elapsed proposed date.

judgments.title: Beanpot hockey tournament — Boston seasonal activity
judgments.description: The annual men's college hockey tournament pits Boston University, Boston College, Harvard and Northeastern against each other at TD Garden; the 74th edition opens on Monday 1 February 2027.
judgments.reason: Recurring scheduled tournament at venue, outcome unknown.

judgments.title: Iroquois Steeplechase — Nashville seasonal activity
judgments.description: A spring horse-racing day and social tradition in Percy Warner Park; the operator lists the race for Saturday 8 May 2027.
judgments.reason: Routine scheduled annual race at park, outcome unknown.

judgments.title: BRP Hemera BESS: 207 MW Battery Storage in Deaf Smith County, Texas
judgments.description: BRP Hemera BESS is a proposed 207 MW (206.96 MW) battery storage project in Deaf Smith County, Texas, in the ERCOT queue as 24INR0134. It would connect at the 345 kV Deaf Smith Substation (Oncor) with a proposed commercial operation date of December 2029.
judgments.reason: Proposed battery queue entry, no execution milestone.

judgments.title: Bee Hollow Solar: 150 MW Solar in St. Clair County, Illinois
judgments.description: Geronimo Power's 150 MW Bee Hollow Solar project in St. Clair County, Illinois began onsite construction in October 2025 and is expected to reach commercial operations in late 2026. It has a power purchase agreement with the Illinois Municipal Electric Agency.
judgments.reason: Construction commenced and power purchase agreement secured.

judgments.title: Timberwolf Solar: up to 100 MW Solar Project in Lodi Township, Mower County, Minnesota
judgments.description: Timberwolf Solar, LLC, a NextEra Energy Resources subsidiary, applied to the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission for a site permit for an up to 100 MW AC solar facility on about 1,113 acres in Lodi Township, Mower County. Public scoping meetings were held on February 20-21, 2024. Its status after February 2024 has not been confirmed from an opened source.
judgments.reason: Permit application and old scoping, subsequent status unknown.

judgments.title: Riverside Solar: 100 MW Solar Project in Lyme and Brownville, Jefferson County, New York
judgments.description: AES's Riverside Solar is a 100 MW solar project in the Towns of Lyme and Brownville, Jefferson County, NY, which received an ORES siting permit on January 9, 2023. Aggregators list a proposed completion of July 2029; AES describes it as in development.
judgments.reason: Siting permit approval and continuing development, no completion.

judgments.title: Delta Bobcat Solar (Lutesville Solar): Up to 200 MW Solar in Cape Girardeau County, Missouri
judgments.description: NextEra Energy Resources' Delta Bobcat Solar is a proposed solar project of up to 200 MW on about 1,200 acres in southern Cape Girardeau County, Missouri. NextEra's project page schedules operations to begin in November 2026 and cites up to 250 construction jobs.
judgments.reason: Proposed project with scheduled operation not confirmed.

judgments.title: Burr Oak Solar: 300 MW Solar in DeKalb County, Illinois
judgments.description: Leeward Renewable Energy's Burr Oak Solar is a 300 MW solar facility on 1,984 acres across Pierce, Afton and Squaw Grove townships in DeKalb County, Illinois, approved by the county board in September 2025. The application says construction could begin in 2027 with a $414 million capital investment.
judgments.reason: County approval is positive progress; construction remains future.

judgments.title: Pine Ridge Solar: up to 300 MW Solar Project near Hardin, Big Horn County, Montana
judgments.description: Pine Ridge Solar is a BluEarth Renewables solar project of up to 300 MW proposed on about 5,800 acres of private land near Hardin, Montana. The developer reports it is in the final stages of the interconnection process, with no firm construction or operation dates published.
judgments.reason: Development/interconnection progress, no firm build or operation date.

judgments.title: Hyco Solar: 80 MW Solar Project in Person County, North Carolina
judgments.description: Hyco Solar LLC is a planned 80 MW solar photovoltaic plant in Person County, North Carolina, operated by Cypress Creek Renewables. EIA-based listings give a proposed completion of November 2027.
judgments.reason: Planned solar project with proposed date only.

judgments.title: Southbury Transfer Station Solar Array (Verogy), New Haven County, Connecticut
judgments.description: The Town of Southbury is working with Verogy on a privately financed solar array on a portion of the transfer station property, with about $35,000 per year in land-lease payments for 20 to 35 years. A public information session was set for April 30, 2026, ahead of Planning Commission review.
judgments.reason: Proposed municipal lease collaboration ahead of review.

judgments.title: Microsoft Becker Data Center: Planned Campus on 295 Acres in Becker, Sherburne County, Minnesota
judgments.description: Microsoft bought about 295 acres in the city of Becker, Sherburne County, from Xcel Energy for about $17.7 million for a future data center. Microsoft has not released details of its plans, and trackers list the project as planned. Third-party trackers cite 325 MW but this is not confirmed by Microsoft.
judgments.reason: Land purchase enables future expansion, plans not disclosed.

judgments.title: Clinton Solar 5: Pivot Energy Community Solar in Clinton County, Illinois
judgments.description: Clinton Solar 5 is a Pivot Energy-linked solar plant listed in Clinton County, Illinois, alongside Pivot's Clinton Solar 2, 2b, 4 and 4b community solar sites. Its capacity and in-service date are not published in the sources found.
judgments.reason: Project listing lacks confirmed capacity and execution date.

judgments.title: Weld Energy Center: 100 MW / 400 MWh Battery Storage near Severance, Weld County, Colorado
judgments.description: Weld Energy Center is a 100 MW lithium iron phosphate battery that discharges over four hours (about 400 MWh), built and operated by a NextEra Energy Resources subsidiary under a long-term agreement with Platte River Power Authority. It sits next to Platte River's Black Hollow Sun solar site and Severance Substation in Weld County. NextEra and Platte River broke ground in June 2026, with operation targeted for late 2026.
judgments.reason: Groundbreaking and long-term contract are concrete expansion progress.

judgments.title: Google Fort Wayne Data Center (Project Zodiac): $2 Billion Campus in Allen County, Indiana
judgments.description: Google's $2 billion Fort Wayne data center campus near East Tillman and Adams Center roads in Allen County, Indiana broke ground in April 2024 and was declared operational in December 2025. Construction continues on the 772-acre, up-to-12-building campus served in partnership with Indiana Michigan Power.
judgments.reason: Campus declared operational, continued expansion.

judgments.title: Burkhalter Road Data Center: 99 MW Data Center in Statesboro, Bulloch County, Georgia
judgments.description: 4AM Development LLC proposes a two-story, 230,000 sq ft data center, described in a lawsuit petition as 99 MW, on 26.49 acres at 6539 Burkhalter Road in Statesboro. The city council approved the rezoning Aug. 18, 2026 and a group sued on Sept. 17.
judgments.reason: Rezoning approval offset by lawsuit challenging project.

judgments.title: Keel Infrastructure Scrubgrass AI Campus: Proposed Data Center (250-750 MW studied) in Venango County, Pennsylvania
judgments.description: Keel Infrastructure, formerly Bitfarms, is exploring an AI data center campus at the Scrubgrass power plant site near Kennerdell in Venango County. It has completed conceptual FirstEnergy load studies at 250, 500 and 750 MW, with the site listed at up to 1.3 GW potential. As of August 2026 a county commissioner said nothing had been filed with the planning department.
judgments.reason: Conceptual studies with no filed proposal, outcome unknown.

judgments.title: Maple Solar: 35 MW Solar Farm in Salamonie Township, Huntington County, Indiana
judgments.description: Maple Solar, LLC told the Huntington County Council and Commissioners in December 2022 that it intends to invest about $45 million in a 35 MW solar farm on roughly 200 acres in Salamonie Township. Cleanview lists the planned project with an expected online date of December 2028.
judgments.reason: Planned investment with future tracker date only.

judgments.title: Scioto Ridge Solar: 110 MWac Solar and 20 MW Storage in Hardin County, Ohio
judgments.description: RWE's Scioto Ridge Solar is a 110 MWac solar project with 20 MW of battery storage in Lynn, McDonald and Taylor Creek townships, Hardin County, Ohio. The Ohio Power Siting Board approved it in August 2024 and RWE lists it as under construction. It is not in Scioto County.
judgments.reason: Permit approval and active construction.

judgments.title: Prairie Oak Solar: 250 MW Solar Project in Shelby County, Illinois
judgments.description: Prairie Oak Solar is a planned 250 MW solar plant in Shelby County, Illinois, operated by Strata Clean Energy, with a proposed online date of September 2027 per EIA-based and Cleanview listings.
judgments.reason: Planned solar plant with proposed online date.

judgments.company: Louisville Gas and Electric (LG&E) and Kentucky Utilities (KU)
judgments.title: E.W. Brown Battery Energy Storage System: 125 MW / 500 MWh BESS in Mercer County, Kentucky
judgments.description: LG&E and KU's E.W. Brown BESS is a 125 MW, 500 MWh battery at the existing E.W. Brown Generating Station in Mercer County, Kentucky, certified by the Kentucky PSC in November 2024. LG&E expected the facility to enter service in the first part of 2027.
judgments.reason: Regulatory certification and targeted service, not confirmed completion.

judgments.title: Glassworks Data Campus: Conceptual 100 MW (up to 700 MW) Data Center Campus in Clarion Borough, Clarion County, Pennsylvania
judgments.description: The Glassworks Data Campus is a conceptual data center plan on about 100 acres in Clarion Borough, backed by the Miles family of companies. Marketing materials cite immediate access to 100 MW of grid power and up to 700 MW with on-site generation. County officials said in January 2026 that no formal proposal had been filed and the concept depends on securing a tenant.
judgments.reason: Concept dependent on tenant and no formal proposal.

judgments.title: Willowbrook Solar I: 150 MW Operating Solar Farm in Highland County, Ohio
judgments.description: Willowbrook Solar I is a 150 MW solar facility in Highland and Brown counties, Ohio, led by RWE and now operating. It was first proposed at 100 MW in an AEP Ohio filing.
judgments.reason: Solar facility now operating.

judgments.title: Chirisa Armstrong Data Center: up to 100 MW Redevelopment at RIDC Armstrong Innovation Park, Armstrong County, Pennsylvania
judgments.description: Chirisa Technology Parks bought the vacant 71,000 sq ft former BNY Mellon data center on a 37-acre site in Freeport, Armstrong County for $5.5 million and plans to redevelop it. Reporting says up to 100 MW could be available on an 18-24 month timeframe once work starts.
judgments.reason: Site acquired for redevelopment, work and power timing prospective.

judgments.title: Fern-Roth Solar: 40 MW Solar Farm near Alexandria, Douglas County, Minnesota
judgments.description: Fern-Roth Solar is a 40 MW solar project by Allied Solar, a joint venture of Greenwood Sustainable Infrastructure and SolarGen, south of I-94 near Alexandria in Douglas County. The county board reviewed it in 2024 and the MISO queue lists it at 39.5 MW; no construction or operation date is published.
judgments.reason: County-reviewed proposed project; construction/operation unconfirmed.

judgments.title: Grandview Solar: 91 MW Solar Project in Spencer County, Indiana
judgments.description: Grandview is a 91 MW solar development in Spencer County, Indiana, acquired by Sol Systems from Orion Renewable Power Resources in June 2022. No construction or online date has been published.
judgments.reason: Acquired solar development, execution dates unannounced.

judgments.title: Homer City Energy Campus: up to 4.5 GW Gas-Powered Data Center Campus in Indiana County, Pennsylvania
judgments.description: Homer City Redevelopment and Kiewit announced in April 2025 a gas-powered data center campus of more than 3,200 acres on the former Homer City coal plant site in Indiana County, with up to 4.5 GW of power. Construction was expected to start in 2025 with power by 2027.
judgments.reason: Large campus announced; future construction/power claims are expectations.

judgments.title: Troy Solar: 50 MW Solar Plant in Troy, Perry County, Indiana
judgments.description: Troy Solar is a 50 MWac solar plant along State Road 545 in Troy, Indiana, serving CenterPoint Energy's Indiana Electric customers and built by Burns & McDonnell. Construction was reported begun in October 2020 with full operation expected in early 2021.
judgments.reason: Construction commenced; stated operation is expected rather than verified.

judgments.title: Ross County Solar: 120 MW Solar Farm in Ross County, Ohio (Operating)
judgments.description: Ross County Solar is a 120 MW solar project operated by Geronimo Power in Ross County, Ohio, listed with its first unit online on January 1, 2025. Geronimo announced the start of operations at Ross and Fayette Solar in June 2025.
judgments.reason: Operator announced commercial operation.

judgments.title: The October Jobs Report Lands November 6, With Kalshi Betting Payrolls Stay Positive
judgments.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the October 2026 Employment Situation at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on 6 November. On 3 November Kalshi priced payrolls above 0 at 82% and unemployment above 4.0% at 94%.
judgments.reason: Routine statistics publication and market expectations, no agency win/loss.

judgments.title: Comcast Files WARN Notices for Nearly 1,000 Layoffs Across Four States
judgments.description: Comcast filed WARN notices from 29 October covering 159 jobs in Washington, 634 in Philadelphia, 119 in New Jersey and 82 in California, about 994 in all, after saying it would book a Q4 restructuring charge of more than US$1 billion.
judgments.reason: Nearly1000layoffs and substantial restructuring charge.

judgments.title: October CPI Lands November 10, With Kalshi Pricing a 0.3% Headline Monthly Band
judgments.description: BLS publishes October 2026 consumer prices at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on 10 November. In the 6 November evening snapshot, Kalshi’s Yes bid/ask was 58–61% above a 0.2% headline monthly increase and 41–43% above a 0.2% core increase. These are market forecasts, not published inflation.
judgments.reason: Scheduled CPI publication and exchange odds, no agency outcome.

judgments.title: Fiserv Says It Has Cut 3,000 Employee and Contractor Roles Since June
judgments.description: On its third-quarter earnings call on 3 November 2026, Fiserv CEO Takis Georgakopoulos said the payments company has reduced contractors and employees by 3,000 since he took over, including more than 10% of senior management, while doubling its Project Elevate savings target to $1 billion.
judgments.reason: 3000employee/contractor reductions; cost-savings target does not negate workforce contraction.

judgments.title: Bracco Announces a $230 Million Sanford Contrast-Media Plant and 200 Jobs
judgments.description: On 27 October 2026 North Carolina Governor Josh Stein and Bracco Imaging announced a $230 million sterile plant in Sanford, Lee County, Bracco's first US factory for injectable contrast media, planned to create 200 jobs backed by a state grant of up to $2.86 million.
judgments.reason: Announced firstUS injectable-contrast factory and expansion, future jobs not realized.

judgments.title: Intel Unveils Gaudi 3 AI Accelerator at Intel Vision 2024
judgments.description: Intel introduced the Gaudi 3 AI accelerator on April 9, 2024 at Intel Vision, a 5 nm part with 24 on-board 200 Gb Ethernet ports that Intel pitched against Nvidia's H100 for enterprise generative AI.
judgments.reason: NewAIaccelerator introduced; no independent victory inferred from maker comparison.

judgments.title: Intel Arc A770 and A750 Desktop Graphics Cards Launch
judgments.description: Intel's first Arc desktop graphics cards went on sale on October 12, 2022: the Arc A770 from $329 and the Arc A750 at $289, taking on Nvidia's GeForce RTX 3060 on price and performance per dollar.
judgments.reason: Desktopgraphics cards released, no review outcome claimed.

judgments.title: Intel Launches Xeon Scalable Processors (Skylake-SP)
judgments.description: Intel launched its Xeon Scalable family on July 11, 2017: more than 50 processors in Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum tiers, up to 28 cores per socket, a six-channel memory controller and AVX-512, aimed at AMD's upcoming EPYC.
judgments.reason: Serverprocessor family launched with expanded offering.

judgments.title: Intel Announces $2 Billion Acquisition of Habana Labs
judgments.description: On December 16, 2019 Intel announced it had acquired Israeli AI chip maker Habana Labs for about $2 billion, adding the Gaudi training and Goya inference processors to its data-center AI portfolio.
judgments.reason: Completed acquisition broadensAIportfolio; companywide deal.

judgments.title: Intel CEO Gelsinger Announces IDM 2.0 Strategy and Intel Foundry Services
judgments.description: On March 23, 2021 Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger announced IDM 2.0: keep most chips in Intel fabs, use outside foundries for some tiles, and launch Intel Foundry Services, backed by two new Arizona fabs at about $20 billion.
judgments.reason: Newfoundrybusiness strategy/investment announced, future execution uncertain.

judgments.title: Amazon Web Services Launches Amazon S3 Storage
judgments.description: On March 14, 2006 Amazon Web Services launched Amazon S3, a simple storage service for developers priced at 15 cents per gigabyte per month, the first service in what became Amazon's cloud business.
judgments.reason: Cloudstorageservice launched.

judgments.title: Amazon Announces EC2 Limited Beta, Renting Servers by the Hour
judgments.description: In late August 2006 Amazon opened a limited public beta of Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), letting developers rent virtual servers at about 10 cents per instance-hour on a first-come, first-served basis.
judgments.reason: Limited publicbeta launched, not fullrelease outcome.

judgments.title: Amazon Launches the First Kindle E-Reader for $399
judgments.description: Amazon released the first Kindle e-reader on November 19, 2007 for $399, and says its initial stock sold out in about five and a half hours; it stayed out of stock until the following April.
judgments.reason: Newreader launch and rapid initialsellout are strong demand evidence.

judgments.title: Amazon Unveils Echo, the Alexa Smart Speaker, by Invitation
judgments.description: On November 6, 2014 Amazon unveiled the Echo, a voice-controlled speaker with the Alexa assistant, priced at $199 ($99 for Prime members for a limited time) and sold by invitation until July 14, 2015.
judgments.reason: Invitation-only speakerannouncement, futuregeneralavailability.

judgments.title: Amazon Completes $13.7 Billion Acquisition of Whole Foods Market
judgments.description: Amazon closed its purchase of Whole Foods Market on August 28, 2017 at $42 per share in cash, about $13.7 billion including net debt, and the grocer's headquarters stayed in Austin, Texas.
judgments.reason: Acquisition completed, positive expansion without claiming payoff.

judgments.title: Nintendo Family Computer (Famicom) Launches in Japan at ¥14,800
judgments.description: Nintendo put the Family Computer, or Famicom, on sale in Japan on July 15, 1983 at ¥14,800: an 8-bit console with interchangeable cartridges that launched Nintendo's home-console line.
judgments.reason: Famicom homeconsole wentonsale; productline normalized tointernationalname.

judgments.title: Nintendo Game Boy Launches in Japan
judgments.description: Nintendo released the Game Boy handheld in Japan on April 21, 1989, a monochrome cartridge-based portable that started the Game Boy line.
judgments.reason: Handheldplatform released.

judgments.title: Super Mario Bros. Released on the Famicom in Japan
judgments.description: Super Mario Bros. went on sale in Japan for the Famicom on September 13, 1985; Nintendo gives October 18, 1985 for its North American release on the NES.
judgments.reason: Game released, no retrospectiverecord outcome used.

judgments.title: Nintendo Super Famicom Launches in Japan at ¥25,000
judgments.description: Nintendo launched the Super Famicom in Japan on November 21, 1990 at ¥25,000; its first shipment of 300,000 units sold out within hours, with Super Mario World and F-Zero as launch games.
judgments.reason: Consolelaunch and300000initialunits soldout withinhours.

judgments.title: Nintendo Game Boy Advance Launches in Japan
judgments.description: Nintendo released the Game Boy Advance in Japan on March 21, 2001, with a North American launch on June 11, 2001 at US$99.99.
judgments.reason: Newgeneration ofGameBoy handheld released; generation removedfrom productline.

judgments.title: The Legend of Zelda Launches on the Famicom Disk System in Japan
judgments.description: The original The Legend of Zelda released in Japan on February 21, 1986 as a launch title for the Famicom Disk System; the NES version followed in North America on August 22, 1987.
judgments.reason: Originalgame/franchise released.

judgments.title: Nintendo 64 Launches in Japan
judgments.description: Nintendo released the Nintendo 64 in Japan on June 23, 1996 at a reported ¥25,000; its North American launch price was US$199.
judgments.reason: Newconsole released.

judgments.title: Nintendo DS Launches in North America at $149.99
judgments.description: The Nintendo DS launched in North America on November 21, 2004 at $149.99, ahead of Japan on December 2, 2004 at ¥15,000, the first Nintendo hardware to launch in North America before Japan.
judgments.reason: Handheldplatform released.

judgments.title: Pokémon Red and Green Released in Japan for the Game Boy
